title: Contingency Placement Agreements — The Early-Termination Charge and Its Booking Instrument
content:
The early-termination charge owed under the Contingency Placement Agreements for a termination notice on record is figured from the tier's early-termination fee and booked on the date the notice was received. The charge concerns the agreement on which the client's termination notice is recorded; it is an entry of that agreement's client money history and part of the fees the client owes Ridgeline on that agreement.

## Business effect of booking

Booking the charge adds one early-termination charge entry to the agreement's client money history, dated the day the client's termination notice was received, and raises the fees the client owes Ridgeline on that agreement by the same amount. The charge then appears in the agreement's money history and in its fees owed.

## Instrument: `book_early_termination_charge_4cc8362c`

**Capability.** One call books one early-termination charge on one creditor client's contingency placement agreement, with the business effect stated above.

**How it is invoked.** The tool is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `book_early_termination_charge_4cc8362c` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `agreement_id` | the placement agreement reference number (agreement id) of the creditor client's contingency agreement being charged, read from the placement agreement lookup | identifier, as the lookup shows it |
| `notice_date` | the date the client's termination notice was received; it becomes the date of the charge entry | calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD, no time zone |
| `charge_amount` | the early-termination charge | USD, always positive, rounded to the nearest cent (2 decimal places) before it is passed |

**Return.** A text receipt of a dictionary with:

- `entry_id` — the reference of the new client money entry;
- `agreement_id` — the agreement charged;
- `entry_type` — always `client_early_termination_fee_assessed`;
- `amount` — the charge booked, USD to 2 decimal places;
- `entry_date` — the notice date, YYYY-MM-DD;
- `fees_owed_after` — the agreement's fees owed once the charge is added, USD to 2 decimal places.

Receiving the receipt means the charge is booked.

## Reference questions

**On which date does the charge entry stand?** On the date the termination notice was received, which is the date passed as `notice_date` — not the day the booking is made.

**What does the instrument check?** The instrument books the figure passed to it; it does not work the figure out.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A call with `agreement_id` set to an agreement's reference number, `notice_date` set to 2026-03-04 and `charge_amount` set to 1234.56 returns a receipt whose `entry_date` is 2026-03-04, whose `amount` is 1234.56, and whose `fees_owed_after` is the earlier fees owed on that agreement increased by 1234.56.
